text.p: Tool and hardware maker Stanley Works will announce a company-wide restructuring in mid-July, company spokesman Gerry Gould said on Monday.

"We plan to announce a company-wide plan for long-term, sustainable, profitable growth for the business," Gould told Reuters in an interview. "An element of it is certainly going to be a restructuring."
Gould was elaborating on information given out at last week's annual shareholders meeting.
He said details were not finalized yet, and declined to comment on possible job cuts or transfers.
Stanley Works will spend more money on advertising and product development, Gould said.
The 154-year-old company is one of the biggest employers in Connecticut, where it employs about 2,000 people. It has about 19,000 employees worldwide.
"We want to become the Coca-Cola of the hard goods industry, meaning that our brand is that ubiquitous and well-known," Gould said.
"We want to have similar recognition on Wall Street as Coca-Cola has."
"People seek out our stock right now because we have a lot of potential for that kind of performance, but we haven't demonstrated it yet."
Stanley Works Chairman and Chief Executive Officer John Trani joined the company last December from General Electric Co, where he was chief executive of GE Medical Systems.
Trani has said he intends to make sweeping changes to boost the Stanley brand name.
Gould said the company's business costs have already come down "considerably" since it began a cost-cutting program in 1995.
"The piece that John Trani brings that we've never had before is some direction on how to grow," Gould said. "He's got a clear vision on how he wants us to grow.
Stanley Works' shares were unchanged at 38-1/8 at 1215 EDT.
